problem: The claim that 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) 'replaces pure contention with OFDMA and scheduled uplinks' is wrong. Wi-Fi 6 still uses CSMA/CA with EDCA contention; OFDMA and trigger-frame uplink scheduling are added on top of it, not in place of it.
fix: 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) keeps CSMA/CA with EDCA and adds OFDMA plus AP-triggered uplink scheduling, so one transmission opportunity can carry several stations at once.

problem: The Wi-Fi name a user picks and that appears in beacon frames is the SSID; ESSID is an older synonym for the identifier of an extended service set. Stating flatly that the ESSID is 'the Wi-Fi name you pick' blurs the term students will meet in the scan and association steps.
fix: The service set identifier (SSID) is the Wi-Fi name you pick from the list; inside an ESS the same name is also called the ESSID.

problem: The pairing of CW = 15 slots with a 20 µs slot does not match a real PHY. In the standard, CWmin = 15 goes with the 9 µs OFDM slot, and CWmin = 31 goes with the 20 µs DSSS slot.
fix: Either use CW = 31 with 20 µs (DSSS/802.11b) or CW = 15 with 9 µs (OFDM), and say which PHY the numbers belong to.

problem: 'A device active in two piconets forms a scatternet' is compressed enough to mislead. The scatternet is the combined set of piconets; the device is the shared node that links them.
fix: A device that belongs to two piconets at once links them; the linked piconets together form a scatternet.
